svg.title: The dqx NVFP4 decode
svg.text: dqx: eight FP4 weights to BF16 in 8 instructions, 5 of them integer-pipe ops
prepare() stores each 32-bit word through an invertible GF(2) map, so the kernel's decode is a few shifts, XORs and masks.
one 32-bit word = 8 NVFP4 codes, in a layout chosen by search
M = 0x81C081C0: each register's 8 lit bits are two
BF16 halves, (s, e1, e0, m) at bits 15/8/7/6 and 31/24/23/22,
which is the E2M1 value x 2^-126 exactly. One bf16x2
multiply by scale x 2^126 then gives the exact product.
Some stored bits are read 3 times and the extra copies
cancel through the XOR partner, so the layout has to be
an XOR mix, not a permutation.
200 paired, role-swapped repetitions each, same GPU, base and seeds. dqx: +0.39% over DQ7, +0.25% over dqm, +0.7 to 1.0% at the large loads.
Removing it from the incumbent later cost 0.72% in a screen: the largest single piece of the incumbent at the time.
the integer pipe was 48% busy, the FMA
72% the public author saw. Moving 2 ops
per word to the FMA pipe relieves part
of it, and the stream is partly
